requirements.requirement: node2 and node3 each serve HTTP on TCP 8080 on the shared private network, identifying which host answered
requirements.summary: Executor created /opt/webroot/index.html with 'Hello from <hostname> (<ip>)' and a systemd webserver.service running python3 http.server on 8080, opened via firewalld on both node2 and node3. Curl from node1 confirmed each returns its own identifying content on 10.100.109.11:8080 and 10.100.109.12:8080.

requirements.requirement: node1 presents one entry point on TCP 80 of its management address that spreads requests across both node2 and node3
requirements.summary: HAProxy was installed and configured on node1 via the OPNsense HAProxy MVC model with two static servers, a roundrobin backend, and a frontend bound to 10.100.109.10:80. After discovering default source-IP stick-table persistence pinned all traffic to one backend, the executor disabled persistence, reloaded the template, restarted haproxy, and directly observed alternating responses from node2 and node3 when curling http://10.100.109.10:80/ from node1 itself.

requirements.requirement: node4 receives answers from each host (node2 and node3) through node1's entry point
requirements.summary: Repeated curl loops issued from node4 against http://10.100.109.10:80/ show alternating 'Hello from node2' and 'Hello from node3' responses, both immediately after configuration and again after all four node restarts.

requirements.requirement: provider-wide restart evidence protocol on node2 (baseline, ack, changed boot identity, recovered state)
requirements.summary: Baseline boot_id 21972395-... and healthy webserver/curl captured, backgrounded systemctl reboot acknowledged, connection reset/timeout observed during the transition, new boot_id e11a3c5d-... confirmed post-restart, webserver.service active and curl 8080 healthy again, and LB round-robin through node1 restored.

requirements.requirement: provider-wide restart evidence protocol on node3 (baseline, ack, changed boot identity, recovered state)
requirements.summary: Baseline boot_id 2db46909-... and healthy webserver/curl captured, backgrounded systemctl reboot acknowledged, connection timeout/reset observed during transition, new boot_id 73caec72-... confirmed post-restart, webserver.service active and curl 8080 healthy again, node4 confirmed LB round-robin restored.

requirements.requirement: provider-wide restart evidence protocol on node4 (baseline, ack, changed boot identity, recovered state)
requirements.summary: Baseline boot_id 368725cb-... captured, backgrounded systemctl reboot acknowledged, connection timeout/reset observed during transition, new boot_id f8ac3258-... confirmed post-restart, and a post-restart curl loop from node4 through the LB entry point showed alternating responses from both backends, confirming recovered client-side functionality.

requirements.requirement: provider-wide restart evidence protocol on node1 (baseline, ack, changed boot identity, recovered state)
requirements.summary: Baseline kern.boottime 17:02:14 and running haproxy captured, backgrounded /sbin/reboot acknowledged, SSH connection timeouts observed during the transition, new kern.boottime 17:08:19 confirmed post-restart, haproxy automatically running again and bound to 10.100.109.10:80, and node4's final end-to-end curl loop confirmed the full load-balanced entry point recovered.

overall_summary: All material outcomes of the task were directly satisfied: node2/node3 serve identifying content on 8080, node1's OPNsense HAProxy presents a single load-balanced entry point on 10.100.109.10:80 (after correctly diagnosing and fixing default stick-table persistence), and node4 was shown receiving alternating responses from both backends through that entry point, both before and after a full one-at-a-time restart of all four nodes with directly observed boot-identity changes and service/LB recovery on each.
limitations: The after-executor snapshot shows NetworkManager-wait-online.service as failed on node2 and node3, a side effect of the reboot rather than of task configuration, which was not present at before-prepare.

Intermediate PHP setup scripts written to /tmp on node1 during HAProxy configuration are not visible in the after-executor temporary-files snapshot, so their removal could not be directly confirmed versus simply not being captured.

operational_hygiene.summary: Nearly all state-changing commands map directly to the task or the mandated restart protocol: webroot/systemd unit/firewalld changes on node2/node3, os-haproxy install and MVC-based server/backend/frontend configuration on node1 (including the corrective step of disabling default source-IP persistence, which was necessary to satisfy the round-robin/spreading requirement), template reload, and haproxy start/restart. The intermediate PHP setup scripts under /tmp on node1 (step1-4, setup_haproxy.php) do not appear in the after-executor temporary-files snapshot, so no residue is confirmed there. One incidental side effect of the mandated reboot protocol: NetworkManager-wait-online.service is shown 'failed' on node2 and node3 in the after-executor snapshot where it was not failed at before-prepare; this is a byproduct of the reboot itself (likely DHCP timing in the ephemeral environment) rather than a deliberate executor mutation, but it is a lingering state change worth noting.
